data.long_meaning: Mu'Aaz is an Arabic name for boys that means 'One who is honored', 'One who is respected'. It is a Quranic name because it is mentioned in the Quran. The name Mu'Aaz carries the meaning “One who is honored” and is chosen by families in Islamic traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Arabic tradition and is also used in English, Urdu, Hindi. Parents who choose Mu'Aaz usually hope their child will grow to embody one who is honored and live with faith, good character and purpose.

data.etymology: Mu'Aaz belongs to the Arabic linguistic tradition and is used in Islamic naming. Its recorded meaning is “One who is honored.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Mu'Aaz total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

in_pashto.name: معاذ

in_pashto.long_meaning: معاذ نوم معنی یې ژغورل شوی یا خوندي دی. دا نوم د عربي ژبې څخه راغلی دی او د الله د حفاظت او ژغورنې سره تړاو لري. معاذ بن جبل يو مشهور صحابي رسول و چې په اسلام کې يې مهم رول ادا کړ.

in_english.name: Mu'Aaz
in_english.long_meaning: The name Mu'Aaz is derived from Arabic roots, meaning 'protected' or 'safeguarded'. It signifies being under Allah's protection and care. Mu'az bin Jabal, a companion of the Prophet Muhammad, was a notable figure in Islamic history, playing a crucial role in the dissemination of Islam.

data.cultural_impact: Mu'Aaz is a name that carries a sense of dignity, respect, and honor. In many Islamic cultures, it is considered a noble name for a child to be given. It is a name that reflects the values of respecting and honoring others, and thus, the child is expected to embody these values in their behavior and actions.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Mu'Aaz has spiritual significance as it is a name mentioned in the Quran. In Surah Al-An'am (6:49), Allah SWT says, "Mu'Aaz bin Jabal (from among the Bedouin Arabs) said: 'O my people, I have indeed quit that which is rejected ( disbelief, sins and evil deeds, etc.) and I have embraced that which is rightly-guided (Islam). Thus follow me, and Allah will bestow His Mercy upon you.' " This verse emphasizes the importance of leaving behind sinful ways and embracing righteousness, a concept central to Muslim beliefs. The name Mu'Aaz thus serves as a constant reminder of this lesson, and the bearer of this name is encouraged to strive towards being a person of honor and respect, both in the eyes of God and society.
